document.title: Gandhi Letter to Reagan, August 3, 1988
document.authors: Rajiv Gandhi, Prime Minister of India
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Soviet Withdrawal from Afghanistan 1989 | National Security Archive
document.note: As the Soviets finished withdrawing half their troops, the radical resistance was organizing and less willing to negotiate. Gandhi warns Reagan against 'encouragement of fundamentalism', saying a fundamentalist regime in Kabul would not serve India or the US and cannot be reconciled with democracy and human rights.

events.description: Reagan writes to Gandhi; letter delivered by Armacost
Gandhi writes letter to Reagan on disarmament and Afghanistan
State Department cable 249966 transmits text of Gandhi's letter to Embassy New Delhi
Armacost and Gandhi exchange views on Afghanistan and Armacost briefs Gandhi on Moscow summit
Reagan sent a letter to Gandhi, delivered by Armacost.
Reagan–Gorbachev summit meeting in Moscow, on which Armacost briefed Gandhi.
Armacost delivered Reagan's letter and exchanged views with Gandhi on Afghanistan and the summit.
Gandhi addressed the UN Special Session on Disarmament and presented a comprehensive disarmament action plan.
Gandhi's letter to Reagan, dated New Delhi, calling for faithful implementation of the Geneva Accords and a nonaligned Afghan government.
State Department cable 249966 relayed the text of the Gandhi letter to the US Embassy New Delhi.

sources_cited: Reagan letter to Gandhi of 9 June 1988
Gandhi speech and Action Plan for disarmament at UN Special Session on Disarmament
key_claims: Gandhi urges faithful implementation of the Geneva Accords by all parties.
Gandhi argues Afghanistan needs a broad-based government of national consensus that stays nonaligned.
Gandhi says Afghans should be left free of outside intervention and interference.
Gandhi asserts a fundamentalist regime in Kabul would not serve Indian or US interests.
